Plugin.Name: Unraid Secretary Office
Plugin.Overview: A small office inside your Unraid server's web UI. Each member of staff looks after one part of the server — the nightly backup, getting things back, snapshots, security, tidying up, the logs — tells you what they noticed and, where it makes sense, lets you act on it; before anything changes they show you what will happen and ask. Mr. Backupsy runs the nightly backup (ZFS/btrfs snapshots, database dumps, a package per app and VM, optional encrypted offsite copies with Kopia — new things stay local until you decide). Mr. Restori brings back databases, folders, whole shares, templates and VM configurations, puts aside what he replaces and can undo every restore; his restore drill proves on throwaway containers that the backups come back. Ms. Snapshotini manages ZFS, btrfs and VM snapshots with schedules and retention. The Night Watchman says how securely the server stands and keeps a watch book of what is different from normal. Ms. Dustdevil knows where everything lies and clears away what nobody uses into a storeroom first. Ms. Protocolli reads every log. Jack Emby looks after EmbyCache and keeps film folders together. The Consultant installs the tools the office relies on with you (Kopia, Fix Common Problems, Prometheus, Grafana). The Team Lead suggests whom to hire, tells you what is left to do and reports to Unraid's notifications. Two servers with the office can keep each other's backups as partner offices, and the Night Watchman also reads what a UniFi router sends to Unraid's syslog server. A search (Ctrl+K) finds every place in the office; English, German, Italian, French and Spanish. A plugin: no container, no account, no cloud of ours, nothing locked.
Plugin.Requires: Unraid 7.3.2 or a newer 7.x (Unraid 8 is not supported yet). The nightly backup's snapshots need pools or array disks on ZFS or btrfs (shares on XFS are backed up without a snapshot); partner offices need ZFS. Offsite copies need a Kopia container — the Consultant can install it.
Plugin.DonateText: Tips keep the office going — a share goes to helmi1987, who wrote Jack Emby's tools, and what goes beyond our costs to animal shelters.
